answer: A practical defense is a rate-limited, stake-weighted reputation kernel: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can submit jobs, and its influence grows only after independent counterparties confirm completed work. Creating a thousand velvet-sounding identities does not multiply voting power, because each new account needs its own stake and verified history. A sybil attacker therefore pays an upfront capital cost, risks slashing for fraud, and must wait through real transactions to earn influence; the nectar is that honest agents gain weight without trusting a central identity registry.
